terms.definition: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true: announcing an effect that is not there. Its probability, fixed by the investigator before the study, is the significance level alpha. It names a decision that did not match reality and never a mistake in the conduct of the study.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-006 defines measurement error as the difference between a measured value and an appropriate reference quantity, which is the sense in which a mis-calibrated meter produces an error. A Type I error contains the same word and reports something else entirely: a correctly executed test on honest data reached a decision that happened not to match the world. No measurement is wrong when a Type I error occurs. The orientation scene names this collision in learner prose before either error term is used, and keeps the measurement sense available.

terms.definition: Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is false: missing an effect that is there. Its probability is written beta, and unlike alpha it is not chosen. It depends on the size of the real effect, the sample size, the variability of the measurement, and the threshold, so it has no single value for a study until an effect size is named.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-008 defines random error as unpredictable variation across repetitions that contributes imprecision rather than a systematic shift. That is a property of measurements and samples. A Type II error is a property of a decision rule: the test looked, and concluded nothing was there while something was. Sampling variation is one of the reasons a Type II error happens, so the two ideas are connected, but they are not the same object and this lesson never uses error in the earlier lesson's sense.

terms.definition: The cut-off a study fixes in advance for rejecting the null hypothesis, written alpha. Setting it at 0.05 accepts a 5 in 100 chance of rejecting a true null. It is a design decision made before the data arrive and is not adjusted in light of them.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-008 introduces hypothesis testing, the p-value, and the threshold a p-value is compared against, and this lesson keeps that meaning unchanged. What is added here is the reading of the threshold as a rate: the proportion of studies of a true null that would reject it. Anything about how a p-value is computed or what it conditions on belongs to the earlier lesson, and this lesson assumes it. The everyday sense of the word describing a result as noteworthy is not used anywhere in this block.

terms.definition: The probability that a test rejects the null hypothesis when a stated alternative is true: power equals one minus beta. It rises with the size of the true effect and the sample size, and falls with the variability of the measurement and with a stricter significance level. A power figure quoted without naming the effect it was computed against describes nothing.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-010 uses power in the algebraic sense, in the relationship y = kx^p where p is the exponent of a power law, and PREM-QNT-001 defines an exponent in the same family of meanings. Statistical power shares nothing with that sense beyond the word: it is a probability between 0 and 1 attached to a study design, and no exponent is involved. The orientation scene names the collision with both the algebraic sense and the everyday sense of force or authority before the term is used.

terms.definition: The magnitude of the difference or association a study is trying to detect, stated in the units of the measurement, for example a 9.0 mg/dL difference in mean fasting glucose. In a power calculation it is a quantity named in advance, chosen because a difference that size would be worth finding, and it is not the difference the study went on to observe.

The value of the reported statistic at which a test switches from not rejecting the null hypothesis to rejecting it. For a two-sided test at a significance level of 0.05 on a difference between means, it sits 1.96 standard errors either side of zero, which for the dinner-timing study is 8.09 mg/dL.

The situation in which a study carries out more than one hypothesis test, so that each additional test is another opportunity for a Type I error and the study's overall chance of at least one false alarm exceeds the level any single test was set at.

The probability of at least one Type I error across a whole set of tests. For k independent tests each at level alpha it equals 1 minus (1 minus alpha) raised to the power k, so five comparisons at 0.05 give 0.226 and twenty give 0.642. Correlated tests give a lower figure, which makes the independent formula a ceiling.

Holding the family-wise error rate near a target by testing each of m hypotheses at the target divided by m, so five comparisons intended to give an overall 0.05 are each judged at 0.01. It works, and it is conservative: the stricter threshold lowers the power of every comparison it is applied to.

A comparison named in the study protocol before the data were seen. Prespecification is what allows a stated false-alarm rate to be believed, because the comparison was not chosen by the results. A comparison selected after looking at the data has an unknown error rate, however it is later described.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-009 defines preregistration as a dated research plan recorded before the relevant outcomes are known, so that planned decisions can be told apart from later changes and exploration. This lesson keeps that meaning and extends what hangs on it: prespecification is what makes the significance level of a comparison a believable number, and the multiplicity arithmetic is what quantifies the damage when it is missing. The earlier lesson's distinction between planned and exploratory analysis is used here without being redefined.

terms.definition: A comparison carried out within part of the study population, such as women over 60 or patients above a body mass index cut-point. Each subgroup is smaller than the whole study, so each has lower power, and examining many of them multiplies the chance that one crosses the threshold by chance alone.
